correctness.rationale: The exact pre-absorption Poisson-cycle embedding has iid finite-variance increments Y=-vT+sqrt(2D) max_j W_j(T) with E Y=(v_c-v)/r. Negative mean gives downward reset positions by the strong law; zero mean gives infinitely negative values by iid finite-variance random-walk oscillation. Positive mean yields a positive exponential supermartingale parameter, and independent previous-cycle increments versus the current downward mark give P(hit) <= e^{-theta x} E e^{theta H}/(1-E e^{-theta Y}); by accessibility of large positions before killing, every x>0 has positive survival probability. The strong law, Poisson count law and Borel-Cantelli within-cycle control establish the conditional speed. Exact N=1,2 and Gaussian maxima asymptotics check boundaries. The standalone finite checker tests constants and mean increments without being used as infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The first-group absorption versus permanent escape phase diagram is a natural central first-passage question for synchronous maximum resetting, with nontrivial competition between drift and group selection. It gives an exact critical force, includes the genuinely delicate equality boundary, an explicit N=2 threshold, a large-group sqrt(log N) law and a survivor-conditioned ballistic speed. These are qualitatively predictive, beyond the previously known v=0 escape or a fixed finite-case computation; no claim of entropy production or general harmonic confinement is made.
